arguments.literal: A finite actor realises a selected outer contract through steps; each step's selected context fits the actor's envelope; the actor's internal path within a step is its own.
Standing: recovered as a composite; the generic statement is reframed from the graph profile's graph functions.

clauses.statement: P0: a finite actor realises a selected outer contract through steps whose selected contexts fit its envelope.

arguments.literal: Subject, representation and interpretation are distinct; meaning holds within a declared context through a declared contract.
Standing: independent. With purpose, identity, evidence and authority fixed, two contracts give one representation two meanings.

clauses.statement: P1: subject, representation and interpretation are distinct; meaning holds within a declared context through a declared contract.

arguments.literal: A selected outcome defines adequacy; interfaces inherit material obligations from the transformation they serve.
Standing: independent. Identical capacity serves opposite purposes.

clauses.statement: P2: a selected outcome defines adequacy; interfaces inherit obligations from the transformation they serve.

arguments.literal: An object's identity is declared (authority, kind, value) and survives admissible change; current state, historical observation and representation identity stay separate; a boundary is a claim with a proof obligation.
Standing: independent. Equal capacity admits identity by persistence or by digest.

clauses.statement: P3: identity is declared and survives admissible change; state, observation and representation identity stay separate; a boundary is a claim with a proof obligation.

arguments.literal: Two steps compose only when the first's result type and judgment satisfy the second's exact declared domain and preconditions; composition retains both identities, intermediate results, judgments, evidence, authority, provenance and stop states.
Standing: independent.

clauses.statement: P4a: two steps compose only when the first's result type and judgment satisfy the second's exact declared domain and preconditions; composition retains both identities, intermediate results, judgments, evidence, authority, provenance and stop states.

arguments.literal: Judgments, residuals, observations and authority decisions the outer contract needs are recorded by the step that produced them.

Standing: derived; reframed from AC-009, AC-013, AC-005, UP-017 and UP-021, whose nine statements of conservation become one obligation with typed instances (authority, residual, judgment, frame, transition, successor claim, evidence by reference); each source clause continues to govern its own scope.

clauses.statement: P4b derives from P0, P2 and the step-produced-facts premise: the producing step records what the outer contract needs.

arguments.literal: A step can meet a condition outside its context and cannot report success on one; its result algebra carries indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis as first-class outcomes and its control model names the next move.
Standing: derived.

clauses.statement: P5 derives from P0, the open-world premise and P6: the result algebra carries non-success outcomes as first class and the control model names the next move.

arguments.literal: Definitions, assumptions, observations, candidate judgments and accepted claims have distinct standing; evidence supports a claim on a basis; authority permits or disposes within scope.
Standing: independent. A bounded actor satisfying all else can still take a green label as acceptance.

clauses.statement: P6: standings are distinct; evidence supports on a basis; authority permits or disposes within scope.

arguments.literal: A revision is made after exposure.

Any post-exposure revision is a declared intervention: it is either a method constituent with its own qualification boundary or a new qualification subject, and it cannot retroactively make the original frozen construction pass.

clauses.statement: Any post-exposure revision is a declared intervention: either a method constituent with its own qualification boundary or a new qualification subject; it cannot retroactively make the frozen construction pass.

arguments.literal: The actor of one step need not be the actor of the next; a later actor may re-acquire declared sources but not a prior actor's private memory.

clauses.statement: The actor of one step need not be the actor of the next and cannot re-acquire private memory.

arguments.literal: A step's output is a candidate until evaluated.

clauses.statement: A step's output is a candidate until evaluated.

arguments.literal: The world is open: a step may meet conditions outside its selected context.

clauses.statement: The world is open.

arguments.literal: P0 presupposes a selected outcome (P2).

clauses.statement: P0 presupposes a selected outcome.

arguments.literal: A document set that requires private validator knowledge, whole-corpus loading or a prior actor's memory fails the benchmark regardless of its content.

clauses.statement: A document set needing private knowledge, whole-corpus loading or prior memory fails the benchmark.

arguments.literal: product.bounded_context identifies the enclosing bounded context of the definition's own product WHAT, or is null when no separate enclosing context is claimed. It is not an exhaustive registry and does not flatten subordinate, peer, composed, tenant, user or runtime contexts into one namespace. Those contexts stay defined by their owning authorities, and every local disambiguation names the exact context in which its resolution applies.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §2 Required definition relations; P1, P3

clauses.statement: product.bounded_context names only the enclosing context of the product's own WHAT; other contexts stay owned elsewhere and are never flattened into it.

arguments.literal: Each definition contains: product: the stable product-definition identity, display name, source-project locator and an explicit bounded-context declaration or null; constitution.stdo: the STDO source repository, the mutable version-line discovery selector, and the exact installed release basis with its deterministic manifest digest; constitution.additional_authorities: every non-STDO constitutional set; constitution.entrypoints: basis-qualified useful reading routes; constitution.agent_bootstrap: the constitutional entrypoint and the marker-managed agent-instruction targets; local_constitution: local axioms, overrides and disambiguations with their owning authority, target, basis and scope, including context-qualified term resolution where applicable; reference_frame_bases: one or more accepted collective reference-frame basis declarations with their admitting authorities and governed scopes; what: the current Intent, Product and specification bindings; how: any shared realisation surfaces and one or more independent build tenants; ticketing: the Goals, ticket, comment and optional sprint carrier bindings; composition: explicit relations to other product definitions; and $schema and kind: the schema locator and the stdo.product-definition discriminator.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §2 Required definition relations; P3, P6

clauses.statement: A product definition carries twelve required relations, from product identity and constitution basis to ticketing, composition and its schema discriminator.

arguments.literal: The overlay owns its locator and relation map; the referenced documents own their content. Repeating source truth inside the JSON creates a rival authority and is non-conformant. A local axiom, override or disambiguation gains no authority from its file category or from being listed in the overlay; every local entry names the URI carrying the local decision, the lawful authority that owns it (Product, requirement, accepted design or other), the clause or ambiguity it overrides or resolves where applicable, and its exact scope. An empty local array explicitly declares that no local entry of that kind is bound; omission is not an equivalent declaration.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §2 Required definition relations, §6 Local constitutional binding; P4b, P6

clauses.statement: The definition locates and never restates source truth; a local entry gains no authority from its file category or overlay listing and names its owning authority; an empty array, not omission, declares none.

arguments.literal: Software is recursive and compositional. A released product may build the next released version of itself, a dependent product, or downstream project artifacts. The roles are distinct objects with distinct identities, substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product, install, artifact and product definition, defined once in FOUNDATIONS §2 (product lineage objects) with their governing rules and the compiler analogy; the product definition is the source project's present-tense surface, not the released artifact and not the builder that happens to be running the build.

clauses.statement: A released product may build its next version, a dependent product or artifacts; the lineage roles are distinct objects defined in FOUNDATIONS §2; the product definition is the source project's present-tense surface, not the released artifact.

arguments.literal: The ordinary configuration holds four distinct frames: user acceptance evaluates the Product outcome from the user's supported frame; end to end evaluates the complete runnable causal realisation of that outcome; integration evaluates one material composition boundary and its interaction population; unit evaluates one module-owned law. They add no role, stage, authority or testing hierarchy; the fan-out assigns claims to evidence. A broader frame cannot make a module-owned law true, and any number of narrower green frames cannot establish an unevaluated Product composition or user outcome. A label such as UAT, E2E, integration or unit has no assurance value without the corresponding frame declaration.
P6, P4a, P1

clauses.statement: The ordinary configuration holds four distinct testing frames and the fan-out assigns claims to evidence; narrower green frames cannot establish an unevaluated Product composition or user outcome; a testing label has no assurance value without the corresponding frame declaration.

arguments.literal: A profile may bind a core mechanism to one of its terms; the binding is declared in the profile with its direction, preserved meaning, narrowed scope and invalidation.
Standing: new (P0 boundary, P1); its shape follows ODD's specialisations of F_P and F_H, which ODD probabilistic compute owns in the graph-native context and carries as their provenance.

clauses.statement: A profile binding is declared with direction, preserved meaning, narrowed scope and invalidation.

arguments.literal: A profile declares its closure decisions' mapping to the core and may not add a core member.

clauses.statement: A profile declares its mapping to the core and may not add a member.

arguments.literal: A profile adds domain obligations, bindings and vocabulary; it imports FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION, EVALUATION and SPEC_METHOD by reference and restates none of them.

clauses.statement: A profile imports the core by reference and restates none of it.

arguments.literal: Progress is accepted material movement toward the selected outcome; prerequisite work names the obligation it enables; preservation and repeated proof are evidence, not new progress; rejected or superseded construction is churn; discovering previously hidden distance revises the forecast and is not negative progress. Paperwork, code volume, test count, commit count and review count are not progress by themselves.

clauses.statement: Progress is accepted material movement toward the selected outcome; preservation and repeated proof are evidence, not new progress; superseded construction is churn; paperwork, code volume, test, commit and review counts are not progress by themselves.

arguments.literal: workspace and governed outcome + accumulated practice and historical failures + available actor capabilities + human judgment -> declared frame set -> bounded evaluations -> conjunction or translation where required -> coverage ledger and residual uncertainty -> empirical frame-set revision.
P6, P2

clauses.statement: A project engages a body of work through a declared frame set, bounded evaluations, conjunction or translation where required, a coverage ledger with residual uncertainty, and empirical revision.

arguments.literal: A projection cannot trim a required member to fit a carrier or budget.

clauses.statement: A projection cannot trim a required member to fit a carrier or budget.

arguments.literal: A prompt, a context packet, a symbolic program or any other representation is a projection of an activated frame, not the frame.
P1

clauses.statement: A prompt, packet or symbolic program is a projection of an activated frame, not the frame.

arguments.literal: Project the closure to the selected context, recording its boundary: the excluded, external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams; material not in the closure stays out; adjacent material does not enter because it exists.

clauses.statement: The projection records its boundary seams; material outside the closure stays out.

arguments.literal: Consumed condition -> required Executive constraint: (1) a valid falsification of a mandatory claim governed by a non-waivable hard stop -> the current promotion boundary blocks, whatever the assigned priority or decision cutoff; (2) a valid finding below the Product-owned decision cutoff, with no hard stop -> no block follows mechanically; the Product-owned policy is applied and any accepted residual is kept explicitly; (3) an observation outside the exact evaluated claim -> bounded repricing or re-entry input; it creates no claim-relative block and no further review round by its severity label; (4) an unsupported or materially incomplete technical assessment -> a capable evaluation is reactivated, or indeterminate is kept; Reviewer evidence is not rewritten.
P6, P5

clauses.statement: A hard-stop falsification blocks; a finding below cutoff blocks nothing mechanically; an out-of-claim observation is repricing or re-entry input; an unsupported assessment is reactivated or kept indeterminate.

arguments.literal: Proportionality is the relation between semantic ambiguity removed and effective reasoning complexity introduced. A method obligation is proportional when its contraction of the admissible interpretation space justifies the additional concepts, relations, projections and evidence an actor must hold together to reach a correct decision.

clauses.statement: Proportionality is the relation between semantic ambiguity removed and effective reasoning complexity introduced; a method obligation is proportional when its contraction of the admissible interpretation space justifies the reasoning complexity it adds.

arguments.literal: Human authority may act directly or through an explicitly admitted bounded proxy. Proxy actor identity and human-authority identity remain distinct; a profile's own surfaces may project the human-authority relation under that profile's term. A proxy grant names its grantor, actor, subject, scope, permitted and excluded decisions, validity, delegation rights, revocation and provenance.
IDENTITY §6 (STDO-UP-004); P6, P3

clauses.statement: A proxy acts under a named bounded grant and its actor identity never becomes the human authority's identity.

arguments.literal: A human decision may be exercised directly or through an explicitly admitted bounded proxy whose grant names its scope and exclusions; a proxy cannot change Product meaning, requirements, governing authority or accepted design; such a change re-enters at its owning relation.

clauses.statement: A proxy acts within a named grant and cannot change Product meaning, requirements, governing authority or accepted design.

arguments.literal: A published entity cut makes the eight admissibility surfaces (identity, boundary, authority, state, evidence, treatment, covariance, ambiguity) visible and traceable, each as a stated value, stated absence or stated non-applicability, and records the basis on which identity was discriminated. Cuts are immutable: revising identity or boundary produces a new cut that supersedes the prior one. Concrete carriers, layouts, schemas and storage topology are consumer realisation; the profile requires that the published surfaces survive and does not select their storage form.
WORLD_MODEL §9 Publishing a cut; P0, P2, P3, P4b, P6

clauses.statement: A published cut shows all eight surfaces and its discrimination basis; revising identity or boundary makes a new superseding cut.

arguments.literal: Qualification binds the exact frame revision, actor envelope, evaluation family, basis class and evidence conditions evaluated. It does not generalise to an unevaluated population by naming the frame generically.
P6

clauses.statement: Qualification binds the exact revision, envelope, family, basis class and evidence conditions and does not generalise by naming the frame.

arguments.literal: The qualification population is every function and failure relation the method claims, each with required representative observations: declare (a frame set derived from workspace, outcome, practices, envelopes, inventory, authority and residual boundary; missing authority or evaluation basis refuses); activate (exact subject, basis and capable actor succeed; stale, ambiguous, topology-mismatched, unauthorised and capability-incompatible activations refuse or return closed pressure); evaluate (representative members of all five results; sensitivity and stability); conjoin (compatible results decide; conflict, basis mismatch, mandatory indeterminacy and veto return conflict, indeterminate or refusal without flattening meaning); translate (preserved coordinates and provenance; explicit loss; mismatch refuses); audit_coverage (evaluation, interaction, authority, failure, capability and independence coverage map to frames or residuals; counts cannot close coverage); revise (failure, mutation, evidence and capability change produce the delta and name every reevaluation); result consumption (a consumer uses one closed result without hidden context; insufficient output fails reconstructability); material composition (a case requiring it declares composition, order, closure, failure and authority conservation; one not requiring it stays uncomposed).
P6

clauses.statement: The population is every claimed function (declare, activate, evaluate, conjoin, translate, audit_coverage, revise, result consumption, material composition) with its representative positive, boundary and falsifying observations.

arguments.literal: Question 1 is answered by family inclusion, not by set membership. An evaluation is within a frame's family when the question it decides is one the frame's declared evaluation family states, at the frame's declared coordinates. Membership of the frame in the frame set, the frame's name, a role label or similar wording of the question does not place an evaluation in the frame's family; an activation of a frame on an evaluation outside its family answers question 1 no, whatever the frame's standing in the set.
P2, P1; RF-001; the material relation drawn is evaluation-to-family inclusion; rc.2 #diagnostic-order, #evaluation, #rf-001-evaluation-relativity, #applicability-and-required-results

clauses.statement: Diagnostic question 1 is answered by family inclusion: the evaluation's question is one the frame's declared family states at its coordinates; set membership, name, role label or similar wording does not place it there, and an activation outside the family answers question 1 no.

arguments.literal: Each clause names the principle that requires it (P0 to P6) and, where it restates or supersedes an rc.2 clause, may carry that clause's route as provenance; a route is never the disposition. The corpus is applicable without the rc.2 cut, which remains the operative builder of this construction until STDO 3 is released.

clauses.statement: Each clause names the principle that requires it and may carry an rc.2 route as provenance, never as its disposition; the corpus is applicable without the rc.2 cut, which remains the operative builder until STDO 3 is released.

arguments.literal: Goals are the current work wave; Product Definition is the present-tense shape of the mutable source project, not the released artifact; requirements state what the project must make true; design chooses how. Read models, commentary and generated views never outrank live specification.

clauses.statement: Read models, commentary and generated views never outrank live specification.

arguments.literal: A read-only evaluation declares no operation authority; an effectful evaluation inherits the exact operation grant from its existing owner, and the frame does not create that grant.
P6

clauses.statement: A read-only evaluation declares no operation authority; an effectful one inherits the exact existing grant, which the frame does not create.

arguments.literal: Before declaring realization_refactor for a bug, establish that the current requirement and the accepted realising design govern the affected behaviour and remain sufficient for the authorised outcome. Their presence proves no coverage. Missing or ambiguous evidence leaves the affected treatment unknown; it is not proof that the governing layer itself is absent.
P6

clauses.statement: realization_refactor for a bug needs an established governing requirement and design; missing evidence leaves treatment unknown.

arguments.literal: An out_of_frame, invalid_basis, repeated indeterminate or incompatible result causes one of: supply the missing admissible evidence; select another actor inside the frame's capability envelope; activate another existing frame; refine or extend a frame declaration; revise the frame set (REFERENCE_FRAME section 10); change the evaluation; or re-enter the governing product or method relation. The disposition follows the cause; a difficult evaluation alone does not prove that another frame is required.
P5, P2

clauses.statement: After out_of_frame, invalid_basis, repeated indeterminate or incompatibility: supply evidence, change actor, activate another frame, refine the declaration, revise the set, change the evaluation, or re-enter; the disposition follows the cause.

arguments.literal: A direct or proxied decision preserves its source, subject and basis, acting identity and mode, scope, change class, disposition and supersession. Recording a ruling cannot widen it. Proxy authority does not make implementer self-review independent and does not confer unrelated runtime or domain authority.
IDENTITY §6 (STDO-UP-004); P6, P4b; EVALUATION §5 applies this law to acceptance

clauses.statement: A recorded decision keeps its coordinates and cannot be widened by recording; a proxy confers no independence and no unrelated authority.

arguments.literal: For a selected activation, measure whether a fresh actor given only the published documents recovers the governing relations with fidelity judged independently, and at what reconstruction cost (context transferred, time, and spend where measurable), against the rc.2 corpus as baseline.
Standing: new; derived from P0 with the actor-change premise.

clauses.statement: The recoverability benchmark measures fresh-actor recovery of the governing relations, judged independently, and its reconstruction cost against the rc.2 baseline.

arguments.literal: A recoverability case gives a fresh actor only this corpus for a bounded activation on a declared subject, with the same task against the rc.2 corpus as baseline; a second case withholds validator folklore, author memory and whole-corpus loading, and the activation still succeeds or returns out_of_frame truthfully.

clauses.statement: Recoverability cases run a fresh actor on this corpus against the rc.2 baseline, with private knowledge withheld.

arguments.literal: A reference conserves a relation when its owner, exact selector, authenticity, availability and completeness support the same consuming decision.
An inaccessible or insufficient reference is a residual, not success.

clauses.statement: A reference conserves a relation when its owner, exact selector, authenticity, availability and completeness support the same consuming decision; an inaccessible or insufficient reference is a residual, not success.

arguments.literal: The refinement rule generalises ODD graph functions, which refine one outer vector into a small inner workflow, to any realisation; PROFILES section 2 keeps the ODD binding. UP-017 and UP-021 are conserved in this section.

clauses.statement: Refinement generalises ODD graph functions to any realisation and conserves UP-017 and UP-021.

arguments.literal: Coverage of the outer obligations, correctness of the local implications and legitimate authority are premises of the induction, not conclusions; 'each step passed' is weaker than 'the outer contract was conserved'.

clauses.statement: Coverage, local correctness and authority are premises; 'each step passed' is weaker than 'the outer contract was conserved'.

arguments.literal: A declared refinement answers a different question, keeps its own vocabulary and declares a total mapping to the core; no refinement adds a core member.

clauses.statement: Each refinement keeps its vocabulary and maps totally to the core; none adds a core member.

arguments.literal: Channel resolution enumerates the published RC tags of the selected namespace (including preserved unqualified historical cuts during a transition), selects the greatest positive ordinal, requires that cut and the current selector to be annotated tags peeling to the same commit, and fails closed when the selector lags or points elsewhere. Channel adoption refuses a same-line target whose ordinal is below the Product Definition's current exact basis; a consumer that intentionally keeps an older cut names that immutable RC URI and digest explicitly and uses exact-basis operations such as sync, not the latest-version channel. Presentation and mutation are separate invocations: the read-only adoption plan binds the current Product Definition bytes and basis to the target immutable cut, annotated tag object, peeled commit, tree and installed-manifest digest and emits a deterministic plan digest; mutation requires that exact digest as the operator's acceptance and re-derives it before changing any Product Definition. Selector, target, manifest or definition drift invalidates the acceptance. A fleet uses one aggregate digest over all exact per-definition plans. Planning inside a mutating invocation is not external presentation and cannot authorise itself.
RELEASE §4; P5, P6, P3; plan hashing and command boundaries are PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4

clauses.statement: Adoption is plan-then-mutate on an exact digest; drift invalidates acceptance; no downgrade through the channel.

arguments.literal: In a shared release source, an immutable cut binds all of: the Project Release Namespace and owning Product authority; the exact qualified Git ref and annotated tag object; the peeled commit and repository-root tree; the normalised repository-relative Project Subtree root at that commit; the Git tree object at that exact Project Subtree root; the declared Product member inventory and release-scoped claim bytes; and the predecessor and successor dispositions required by §9. The Project Subtree root is a locator inside the exact peeled commit, not Product identity. Its canonical spelling is the slash-separated Git path from the repository root, with no leading or trailing slash and no empty, . or .. component; . alone denotes the repository root. Moving a source project changes this locator and its cut identity without reassigning the Project Release Namespace. A tag over a monorepo commit does not make sibling subtrees Product members. Unrelated sibling bytes remain carrier state outside the declared Product subject. Conversely, a member inventory or payload digest without the qualified ref, commit, Project Subtree root and Project Subtree tree is not a complete reacquirable release identity.
RELEASE §2 Project-subtree release identity; P3, P6

clauses.statement: An immutable cut binds ref, tag object, commit, subtree root and tree, inventory, claims and dispositions; an inventory digest alone is not release identity.

arguments.literal: Qualification binds: namespace, qualified immutable RC ref, annotated tag object, peeled commit, repository tree, subtree root and tree, and declared Product member set; the exact release-scoped claim bytes; the governing Product and release basis; each claimed property and its observation boundary; evidence subjects, owner verdicts and unresolved gaps; and the complete successor relation to the declared predecessor (§9). Evidence matches the claim: source success does not prove packaged or installed behaviour, packaging equivalence does not prove semantic behaviour, artifact presence does not prove usability unless presence is the exact claim. An RC is accepted only when the required exact-cut review and operator checks are complete and the human authority accepts that exact subject. If review requires any qualifying-byte change, the verdict stays attached to the old RC and a higher RC is published. Acceptance does not move or rewrite the selector or create another final carrier.
RELEASE §3 Exact-cut qualification; P6, P3, P1; EVALUATION §1 is the generic claim law

clauses.statement: Qualification binds the exact cut, claims, basis, evidence and successor relation; acceptance is the human authority's verdict on that exact subject.

arguments.literal: The release process has three phases: (1) mutable candidate construction; (2) immutable RC publication and monotonic version-line advancement; (3) exact-cut qualification, acceptance and explicit consumer adoption. There is no second final cut after an accepted RC. Publication immediately makes the new highest ordinal discoverable through the selector; acceptance is a verdict over the exact immutable RC, not a second carrier. If any byte capable of affecting the Product or a release-scoped claim changes, the project publishes and reviews a higher immutable RC instead.
RELEASE §3; P0, P3, P6

clauses.statement: Three phases; acceptance is a verdict on the exact RC; any qualifying-byte change means a higher RC, never a second final cut.

arguments.literal: Project qualification is prospective. Existing unqualified refs keep their names, objects, peels and public links; a historical tag object may gain an archival ref but is never recreated, re-annotated, moved or replaced. Public logical release URIs stay unchanged (a logical STDO release remains stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/; the qualified Git ref is transport identity and is not inserted into the URI); resolution binds the logical cut to its exact Git ref and fails closed if one project-local coordinate names different tag objects. Across the transition, latest is the greatest positive RC ordinal over the project's preserved historical and qualified cuts; the first qualified publication creates the qualified selector; the historical unqualified selector stays at its object, ceases to be current for the shared source and is not force-moved.
RELEASE §2 Historical ref and public-URI conservation; P3, P4b, P5

clauses.statement: Qualification is prospective: historical tags and public URIs are conserved; latest spans historical and qualified cuts.

arguments.literal: The release-publication context distinguishes seven identities: Project Release Namespace (stable key assigned by the Product release authority to one independently released source project); Project Subtree (exact repository-relative project root and Git tree object for one cut); Candidate Source (mutable state constructing a possible successor); RC Branch (mutable project-qualified carrier for the current candidate window); Immutable RC Cut (annotated project-qualified tag plus exact Product release subject; names one published candidate and, once accepted, one released Product; it realises the release cut); Version-Line Selector (mutable project-qualified tag alias naming the highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut for that project and version line); Release Branch (optional mutable convenience carrier aligned to the selector's commit). Equal version text does not collapse these identities. Branches and the selector may move. An immutable RC tag never moves.
RELEASE §2; P3

clauses.statement: Seven release identities are distinct; branches and the selector may move, an immutable RC tag never moves.

arguments.literal: Release criteria, immutable release-cut publication, selector advancement and the process for cutting a release belong to RELEASE §2 to §8. Layer and release separation holds (AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §7): a calculus, its interpretation of a subject and its carrier encoding keep independent content identities, judgments, supersession relations and proof obligations, and none is automatically an independently released product.

clauses.statement: Release mechanics belong to RELEASE §2 to §8; a calculus, its interpretation and its carrier encoding keep independent identities, judgments, supersession relations and proof obligations.

arguments.literal: During candidate construction: bounded fixes are allowed after intake triage; qualification and operator review may continue; release notes may stay draft until RC publication; the RC branch may move; mutable source is explicitly non-operative for released consumers. The intended Product boundary, release-scoped claims, excluded source-project state and qualification basis become explicit before RC publication. A material scope change is repriced, not silently absorbed.
RELEASE §3 Mutable candidate construction; P0, P2, P6

clauses.statement: Candidate source may move but is non-operative; boundary, claims and basis become explicit before publication.

arguments.literal: To publish it, the project: 1. confirms the triaged scope and lawful constitutional re-entry; 2. declares the exact Product release subject and release-scoped claim set; 3. reconciles the release note and other release-facing assets to that subject; 4. runs the proportionate pre-RC qualification and operator checks; 5. commits the exact carrier; 6. resolves and records the exact Project Release Namespace, Project Subtree root and Project Subtree tree; 7. creates one annotated immutable <project>/v<version>-rc.<n> tag and an annotated <project>/v<version> selector tag over that same commit in a shared release source; 8. atomically pushes the carrier, RC branch, immutable RC tag, selector and optional release branch where the transport supports it; 9. verifies remotely that the immutable tag, selector and release branch resolve to the highest published RC commit; and 10. records enough ref, subtree, identity and inventory evidence to reacquire the cut without trusting a mutable checkout. Each published RC tag is immutable. Further work increments <n> on the same version line when the intended line remains applicable. It does not require a minor-version increment merely because review found a bounded repair. A published higher RC without matching selector advancement is an invalid, fail-closed release state; it never authorises resolution of the older cut as the version-line latest.
RELEASE §3 Immutable RC publication; P3, P5, P6

clauses.statement: RC publication is ten steps ending in reacquirable evidence; RC tags are immutable and repairs take a higher ordinal.

arguments.literal: <project> is one explicit Project Release Namespace matching [a-z0-9]+(?:[-_][a-z0-9]+)*, with no slash, unique within the release source, stable for the release line and assigned by the Product release authority; a directory name, display name, definition label, package name or matching version cannot infer or reassign it. A shared release source uses for every future publication: RC branch refs/heads/rc/<project>/<version>; immutable RC cut tag refs/tags/<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>; version-line selector refs/tags/<project>/v<version>; release branch refs/heads/release/<project>/<version>; it does not publish a future cut or selector under unqualified v<version>-rc.<n> or v<version>. A single-project source may keep the unqualified profile only while it has exactly one independently released project and its release record declares that profile; adding a second project requires qualified refs before either publishes another cut. Namespaces distinguish refs; they do not merge Products or imply dependency or composition.
RELEASE §2 Project-qualified Git refs; P3, P6

clauses.statement: Release refs carry an authority-assigned project namespace; a shared source never publishes new unqualified cuts or selectors.

arguments.literal: Advancement: (1) identify the new immutable RC tag, ordinal and peeled commit; (2) confirm no higher ordinal exists on the line; (3) confirm the qualified selector is absent or resolves to a lower ordinal on the same project line; (4) atomically create or force-update the annotated <project>/v<version> selector to the new highest RC commit; (5) create or update release/<project>/<version> to the same commit when used; (6) push carrier, RC branch, RC tag, selector and optional release branch atomically where supported; (7) verify remotely that the selector peels to the highest RC commit and the matching immutable annotated RC tag exists. Advancement is refused when the target has no matching immutable annotated RC tag, any higher ordinal exists, the selector would move to a lower RC, or selector and release branch would not align to the same highest commit. Movement is strictly monotonic by ordinal: a later defect is repaired through a higher immutable RC, never by moving an old RC tag or rolling the selector back. The selector equals v<version>-rc.latest; every concrete RC tag stays addressable.
RELEASE §3 Monotonic version-line advancement; P3, P5

clauses.statement: The selector moves only forward to the highest published RC; defects are repaired by a higher RC, never by moving tags back.

arguments.literal: The version-line selector answers only: which highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut currently exists on this version line? It never answers: which exact cut governs this consumer? A Product Definition may keep stdo://channels/<version> as its discovery selector, but its operative basis is the exact stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/ URI and installed-manifest digest. Moving the Git selector updates no consumer. Adoption is a separate explicit Product-Definition transition that resolves, presents, installs, verifies and pins the selected immutable RC. Resolution requires an annotated selector with a distinct peeled commit; absence of a peeled selector ref fails closed and is never read as a lightweight selector.
RELEASE §4; P6, P3, P5; PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4 installed release basis

clauses.statement: The selector names the highest published RC, never a consumer's cut; the operative basis is the exact URI and manifest digest; moving the selector updates no consumer; adoption is a separate explicit transition.

arguments.literal: A successor identifies the exact predecessor immutable RC whose semantic claims it evolves; that origin stays immutable for the candidate. Every predecessor claim capable of affecting the successor receives one semantic disposition: conserved (the successor retains the claim); superseded (an accepted successor relation replaces it); intentionally removed (current Product authority removes it); or not applicable (no successor effect, with a bounded reason). An unresolved disposition blocks qualification of the affected claim. Conservation is semantic: patch absence does not prove loss when a successor-native realisation preserves behaviour, and naming or code similarity does not prove conservation without relevant evidence. Where a maintenance or support line may affect retained claims, the release basis identifies the watched source, observation boundary, inclusion policy and successor candidate; relevant changes receive semantic disposition at material integration and at exact-cut qualification. The consumer owns its record, branch strategy, comparison and proof mechanism.
RELEASE §9 (STDO-UP-015); P4b, P3, P6, P1

clauses.statement: A successor names its exact predecessor RC and disposes every affecting claim; an unresolved disposition blocks the affected claim's qualification.

arguments.literal: Report volume is not model traffic; transferred context is counted across every delegated actor, not only the coordinator.

clauses.statement: Report volume is not model traffic; transferred context counts across every delegated actor.

arguments.literal: Equal representations do not establish equal meaning; meaning is supplied by a declared interpretation contract within a declared context.

clauses.statement: Equal representations do not establish equal meaning.

arguments.literal: Residual = {id, subject, kind, uncertainty, consequence, context, owner, scope, basis, re_entry, invalidation}. Projection, compression, interpretation or encoding cannot erase a residual: it remains represented, is explicitly dispositioned by competent authority, or causes refusal. An undeclared residual kind or value refuses structural admission.
P4b, P6, P3

clauses.statement: A residual record survives projection, compression, interpretation and encoding until competent disposition, or refuses.

arguments.literal: A material uncertainty, omission, loss or unproven relation remains a residual until an authorised disposition.

clauses.statement: A residual remains until an authorised disposition.

arguments.literal: A preservation checkpoint may retain unfinished or unaccepted work under an existing exact operation grant; it identifies its parent or predecessor, the included territory, the concurrent-writer disposition and the durable evidence location, and it is neither acceptance, promotion nor publication. A proposed restart, which reconstructs from less than the retained work, identifies why repair of retained work is insufficient, which obligations and evidence survive, and which causal assumptions change; reconstructability alone does not select reconstruction.
Standing: conserves UP-020 checkpoint and continuation.

clauses.statement: A preservation checkpoint may retain unfinished or unaccepted work under an existing exact operation grant; a proposed restart identifies why repair of retained work is insufficient, which obligations and evidence survive, and which causal assumptions change.

arguments.literal: One core algebra of exactly these five members serves every evaluation and every step's stop state.

clauses.statement: One core algebra of five members serves every evaluation and stop state.

arguments.literal: Resumption does not imply idempotence: an action whose external effect may have occurred is not repeated blindly; the lawful results are reconciliation, yield or stop.
Standing: new (P5 with the open-world premise).

clauses.statement: An action whose effect may have occurred is not repeated blindly; reconcile, yield or stop.

arguments.literal: Resumption is re-entry of the same method over current work state by a possibly different actor. It recovers applicable progress, re-checks the invalidators of each reused result, reopens only affected support, and reconciles uncertain external effects before any repetition.
Standing: the invalidator re-check conserves Return A Closed Result; reconciliation of uncertain external effects is new (P0, P5 with the open-world premise).

clauses.statement: Resumption recovers progress, re-checks invalidators, reopens only affected support and reconciles uncertain effects before any repetition.

arguments.literal: A step's return goes to its declared consumer; in a coordinated configuration that consumer is the executive relation, which consumes closed results, applies disposition under existing decision authority and selects the next authorised action.

clauses.statement: A return goes to its declared consumer; an executive consumes closed results, disposes under existing authority and selects the next authorised action.

arguments.literal: Reusing the constructor's judgment does not satisfy independence; shared mechanical evidence may be reused, judgment may not.

clauses.statement: Mechanical evidence may be reused; judgment may not.

arguments.literal: A reused judgment does not satisfy a separately required independent judgment; the independent assessor acquires its own evidence and supplies its own judgment.

clauses.statement: A reused judgment never satisfies a required independent judgment.

arguments.literal: It may recommend a disposition, which is evidence only and never a disposition; it does not apply one.

clauses.statement: A review may recommend a disposition, which is evidence only; it does not apply one.

arguments.literal: A review returns one core result for each declared predicate it evaluated, with the exact subject and basis, the evidence consulted, the findings ranked by consequence, each finding's evidence and smallest bounded correction, the residual uncertainty and the invalidation conditions.

clauses.statement: A review returns one core result per predicate with subject, basis, evidence, ranked findings, residual uncertainty and invalidation conditions.

arguments.literal: A revision may: clarify activation or evidence acquisition; change the capability envelope; add or remove a material relation; split an overloaded frame; merge duplicative frames where capability and authority stay sound; add intentional overlap; add or revise a conjunction or translation; retire a frame whose evaluation family is no longer material; or revise the project evaluation inventory.
P4b

clauses.statement: Revision actions: clarify activation or evidence acquisition; change the envelope; add or remove a material relation; split; merge where sound; add overlap; add or revise conjunction or translation; retire a frame; revise the inventory.

arguments.literal: Stated plainly: a material revision of a frame produces a new frame revision coordinate. Every prior closed result bound to the previous revision of a materially revised frame is bound to a mismatched coordinate (RF-005) and is invalidated for reuse until it is re-checked against the new revision. The revision record lists those results as reopened; a result leaves that list only by a recorded re-check that finds it demonstrably independent of the change, or by re-evaluation on the new revision. A material revision does not select which of the results bound to the prior revision it reopens, and silence does not keep a result closed. A non-material revision, for example one that clarifies an activation or acquires evidence without changing any declaration, produces no new coordinate and reopens no result; the revision record states that the revision is non-material.
P3, P4b; RF-005, RF-011, ACTIVATION section 7; rc.2 #revision-actions, #rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates, #return-a-closed-result

clauses.statement: A material frame revision reopens every closed result bound to the prior revision coordinate; a result leaves the reopened list only by a recorded re-check finding it demonstrably independent or by re-evaluation on the new revision; silence keeps nothing closed; a non-material revision reopens no result.

arguments.literal: Every frame declares the evaluation family it supports. A frame with no declared evaluation family has no testable sufficiency boundary.
P2

clauses.statement: RF-001: every frame declares its evaluation family; without one it has no testable sufficiency boundary.

arguments.literal: An activated frame contains a finite attention surface that fits the selected actor's declared capability envelope. A frame that needs undeclared ambient memory, conversation history or an effectively global workspace context is not reconstructable for that actor. ACTIVATION section 2 measures the fit where the contract selects measurement.
P0

clauses.statement: RF-002: an activated frame's attention surface is finite and fits the actor's envelope; ambient memory, history or global context make it non-reconstructable.

arguments.literal: Every known relation whose lawful change can alter the evaluation result, the validity of the basis, the sufficiency of evidence, operation authority or decision authority appears in the frame or enters through a declared authoritative input. Omitting a material relation makes the frame insufficient. The law does not require proving that no undiscovered material relation exists.
P2; P0 with the open-world premise

clauses.statement: RF-003: every known material relation is in the frame or enters through a declared input; omission makes the frame insufficient; no proof of no undiscovered relation is required.

arguments.literal: Relations that cannot affect the declared evaluation stay outside active attention unless they are needed to establish that irrelevance. A frame does not expand because adjacent workspace material exists.
P2

clauses.statement: RF-004: irrelevant relations stay out unless needed to establish irrelevance; adjacency does not expand a frame.

arguments.literal: Every result binds its exact subject, basis, coordinates and evidence scope. A stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis returns invalid_basis or requires reactivation. Apparent equality never substitutes for declared coordinate equality.
P3, P1

clauses.statement: RF-005: every result binds exact subject, basis, coordinates and evidence scope; a stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis returns invalid_basis or requires reactivation; apparent equality never substitutes for declared coordinate equality.

arguments.literal: A frame carries and applies admitted authority. It does not mint, widen, transfer or reconstruct semantic, evaluation, operation or decision authority from actor identity, available capability, evidence shape, implementation reachability or frame selection.
P6

clauses.statement: RF-006: a frame carries admitted authority and mints, widens, transfers or reconstructs none from identity, capability, evidence shape, reachability or selection.

arguments.literal: Semantic law defines what the evaluation means; evidence supplies observations; the evaluator applies the declared relation; where the evaluation performs a material operation the existing operation owner supplies the exact grant; decision authority disposes the result. A frame declaration keeps these roles distinguishable even when one actor lawfully performs several of them. EVALUATION section 2 applies this to review.
P6

clauses.statement: RF-007: semantic law, evidence, evaluator, operation grant and decision authority stay distinguishable in a frame even when one actor holds several.

arguments.literal: Frames may share entities, variables, evidence or coordinates. Shared material establishes neither identical meaning nor identical basis, authority or result. Every cross-frame equality or translation an evaluation uses is declared where it is used.
P1, P3

clauses.statement: RF-008: shared material establishes no identity of meaning, basis, authority or result; every cross-frame equality or translation is declared where used.

arguments.literal: Frames may relate through disjointness, overlap, refinement, restriction, translation, temporal succession, composition or governance. Parent and child relations apply only where explicitly declared. Functional decomposition, authority precedence, frame configuration, subject topology and evaluation dependency are distinct relation structures; a consumer may align them where the subject warrants it and may not silently treat them as one hierarchy.
P3, P1

clauses.statement: RF-009: parent and child relations apply only where declared; decomposition, authority precedence, configuration, topology and evaluation dependency are distinct structures never silently treated as one hierarchy.

arguments.literal: Using several frames does not require composing their internal manifolds. Composition law is required only when the governing evaluation combines their internal variables, transports evidence or values across them, or treats their operations as one material execution relation. Independently activated evaluations may instead return closed results to one declared conjunction or decision rule.
P4a

clauses.statement: RF-010: several frames need no composed manifold; composition law is required only when an evaluation combines variables, transports values or treats operations as one; otherwise closed results go to one declared conjunction.

arguments.literal: An activated frame declares the topology changes capable of invalidating its coordinates or its materiality judgment. A detected material topology mutation causes reevaluation, frame revision or recharting before the previous result is reused. Material revision of the frame itself invalidates for reuse every result bound to the prior revision coordinate; §10 Revision actions states that rule.
P3, P4b

clauses.statement: RF-011: an activated frame declares the topology changes that can invalidate it; a detected material topology mutation causes reevaluation, revision or recharting before reuse; material revision of the frame itself invalidates for reuse every result bound to the prior revision coordinate.

arguments.literal: Every evaluation returns a member of its declared result algebra. A performed evaluation returns a member; an evaluation not performed because a declared capability was not exercised owes the step's stop state, not a member (ACTIVATION §3, third case). The core algebra is defined once, in ACTIVATION §3: satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis, with the meanings and the no-coercion rule given there; this member does not define it a second time. An externally owned compatible extension may refine that algebra while preserving explicit indeterminate, out-of-frame and invalid-basis pressure; it may neither add a core member nor coerce one to success.
P5

clauses.statement: RF-012: every evaluation returns a member of its declared algebra; a performed evaluation returns a member, an evaluation not performed because a declared capability was not exercised owes the step's stop state; the core algebra is defined once in ACTIVATION section 3; extensions preserve non-success pressure and add no core member.

arguments.literal: A fresh competent actor inside the declared capability envelope can reconstruct the activated evaluation from the frame declaration, the exact subject, the basis and the admissible inputs, without undocumented conversational or historical context.
P0 with the actor-change premise

clauses.statement: RF-013: a fresh competent actor reconstructs the activated evaluation from declaration, subject, basis and admissible inputs, without undocumented history.

arguments.literal: Frame adequacy includes actor usability. When the material manifold exceeds an actor's capability envelope, human authority may select another actor, refine the frame, sequence activations or provide a lawful compression (RF-017); the selection is human authority's, exercised directly or in advance through the grant, and ACTIVATION section 2 says which of these a step selects itself and which re-enter the grant's owner. The actor may not silently omit material relations to fit its context.
P0, P5

clauses.statement: RF-014: when the manifold exceeds the envelope, human authority (directly or through the grant) selects another actor, refinement, sequencing or lawful compression; silent omission is forbidden.

arguments.literal: Coverage and evaluation results retain known uncertainty. Unresolved relations, uncovered evaluations, contested evidence and unknown capability stay explicit. Absence of a recorded counterexample is not evidence of universal completeness.
P4b, P6; open-world premise

clauses.statement: RF-015: results and coverage keep known uncertainty explicit; no recorded counterexample is not completeness.

arguments.literal: REFERENCE_FRAME requires the declared relations and the observable outcomes. It requires no frame runtime, universal carrier, registry, controller, prompt format, repository layout, collaboration topology, worker count or software framework.
P2

clauses.statement: RF-016: the member requires declared relations and observable outcomes, not any runtime, carrier, registry, controller, format, layout, topology or framework.

arguments.literal: A frame compresses accumulated practice when its declaration preserves the material distinctions and failure detections its evaluation family requires while fitting its capability envelope. Compression does not require a unique smallest frame. Intentional overlap is retained where it supplies independently activated evaluation, different capability fit, different evidence altitude or useful fault detection. Frames are merged only when the merged frame preserves evaluation meaning, authority, capability fit and proportional reasoning cost.
P2, P0

clauses.statement: RF-017: a frame compresses practice when it preserves required distinctions and failure detections within its envelope; no unique smallest frame; useful overlap is retained; merge only when meaning, authority, fit and cost are preserved.

arguments.literal: Constructor, assessor and decision owner are relations an actor occupies over steps, not kinds of actor; no role name confers an operation.

clauses.statement: Roles are relations an actor occupies, not kinds of actor; no role name confers an operation.

arguments.literal: A role, persona, abstraction or component may help construct or activate a frame and none is a reference frame by identity alone; one component may appear in several frames and one frame may cross several components.
P3, P6

clauses.statement: No role, persona, abstraction or component is a frame by identity alone; components and frames cross freely.

arguments.literal: A reader selects the route for their purpose (understand the method; do a bounded piece of work; review someone's work; decide acceptance or release; apply the method to a domain; load it into a model's context) and reads the named documents and sections in order; the document map names which file owns which obligations.

clauses.statement: A reader follows the route for their purpose; the map says which file owns what.

arguments.literal: Builder projects may work a bounded source-object set repeatedly until the resulting attribute ledger is judged sufficiently saturated for publication. Sufficient saturation means: materially important attributes have traceable support; remaining gaps are explicit ambiguities rather than silent misses; and the resulting object cut is stable enough to publish and supersede later if needed. Sparse first publication remains lawful (§9 Admissibility); silent unsupported attribute creation does not.
WORLD_MODEL §11 Saturation law; P2, P5, P6

clauses.statement: Sufficient saturation means material attributes have traceable support and remaining gaps are explicit; sparse first publication remains lawful, silent unsupported attribute creation does not.

arguments.literal: Every seam crossing the affected set includes its far side or states why it cannot participate.

clauses.statement: Every seam crossing the affected set includes its far side or states why it cannot.

arguments.literal: These considerations create no universal resource ledger, benchmark, budget or measurement gate. A resource control applies only through an explicitly selected frame and its owning applicability and work scope; ACTIVATION section 6 is that selection where capability fit or a cost claim is the governed question. Frame selection cannot waive another applicable semantic, authority, evidence or independence constraint.
P2, P6

clauses.statement: Selection creates no universal ledger, benchmark or gate; cost applies only through a selected frame (ACTIVATION section 6); selection waives no other constraint.

arguments.literal: A constructor's self-review is construction output, not assessment.

clauses.statement: Self-review is construction output, not assessment.

arguments.literal: Without an explicit cross-context relation: Frame (reference-frame evaluation context vs a consumer-owned runtime carrier) remains distinct, nominal match cannot enrol the runtime carrier as an evaluation frame; Owner (generic specialist evaluation family vs a semantic or decision authority owner) remains distinct, the family acquires no owner authority; Product (immutable released Product vs mutable Product Definition) remains distinct and selects only through the occurrence's declared context; Tenant (STDO build realisation vs hosted, customer, account, runtime or data tenancy) remains distinct, build tenancy supplies no default; User (Product role, human person, identity principal, account, actor, operator or data subject) is unresolved until downstream authority defines or explicitly relates the meanings. A positive local case declares one context and resolves exactly one concept; a positive cross-context case supplies the complete authorised relation. Negative cases: zero candidates, multiple candidates after disambiguation, a selected concept outside the candidate set, a context-free glossary fallback, incomplete relation coordinates, authority or basis mismatch, undeclared loss and invalidated relations. Correct downstream behaviour produced through a guessed meaning does not pass semantic conformance.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §10 Semantic-resolution conformance cases; P1, P6

clauses.statement: Colliding terms stay distinct without an authorised relation, and behaviour reached through a guessed meaning fails semantic conformance.

arguments.literal: Several realisations may conform to one Σ; sufficiency does not require unique derivation or equality with an incumbent.

clauses.statement: Several realisations may conform to one Σ; sufficiency needs neither unique derivation nor incumbent equality.

arguments.literal: Severity grades the consequence if the finding manifests. Priority orders the response relative to the complete Product outcome, likelihood and exposure, the current MVP or release mandate, reversibility, dependencies, cost of delay and available capacity. The Reviewer grades severity; the Executive assigns priority. The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis binds the severity scale, the priority scale, the current-boundary decision cutoff and the non-waivable hard stops; this profile imposes no universal numeric scale. Severity, priority, the frame result and the current-boundary effect are four distinct values; none of them alone makes a finding release-blocking.

clauses.statement: Severity (Reviewer), priority (Executive), frame result and boundary effect are four distinct values; none alone makes a finding blocking.

arguments.literal: A change alters a load-bearing shared contract.
It is a migration, not a patch: change the authoritative contract first, audit every producer and consumer, migrate each, and chase every downstream effect before declaring completion.

clauses.statement: A load-bearing shared-contract change is a migration: contract first, audit and migrate every producer and consumer, chase every downstream effect.

arguments.literal: Computational similarity yields a commonisation candidate, never an adjudication of identity or authority; one implementation may serve many instances while each instance keeps its responsibility and binding.

clauses.statement: Shared machinery is a commonisation candidate, never an adjudication of identity or authority.

arguments.literal: Silent omission to fit is never one of them.

clauses.statement: Silent omission to fit is never one of the options.

arguments.literal: DESIGN_MODULE is the software-design profile. It imports the core and binds: ontology-first derivation of operation identities from discovered functionality through logical completeness, Prime contraction, the irreducible architectural carrier set and its projections; proportional design sequencing with the decision-complete design gate; bounded frame conservation; native constructability; capability and foundation selection; transformation admission completeness; invariant reconstruction sufficiency; computational realisation projection; the module taxonomy and realisation rules; and the design review questions and checklist. The per-boundary cost of the derivation chain is decided there (DESIGN_MODULE §5 Proportional design sequencing, §7 Gate and retrospective work).

clauses.statement: DESIGN_MODULE is the software-design profile; it imports the core and binds the design obligations; the per-boundary cost of the derivation chain is decided there.

arguments.literal: Sparse first publication remains lawful. A unique, historical, single-context, inaccessible or regulated entity is publishable when the admissibility test holds and its residual ambiguity is declared. Absence of a comparison population, of repeated contexts, or of permission to intervene is a bound on evidence altitude to be stated, not a bar to publication.
WORLD_MODEL §9 Admissibility; P2, P5

clauses.statement: A sparse cut is publishable when the test holds and its evidence-altitude bound and residual ambiguity are stated.

arguments.literal: Capability fit or a cost claim is the governed question.
The activation declares its allowance and reports spend with its measurement source, or records that the counter is unavailable.
Standing: new (P0 with UP-014's selection rule).

clauses.statement: Spend is reported with its measurement source, or the counter is recorded as unavailable (new in this corpus).

arguments.literal: For candidate_ready, the Executive verifies the exact subject and decides whether independent assessment is required by EVALUATION section 3, ACTIVATION section 1, EVALUATION section 7 (method qualification), Product, release, risk or the admitted work contract. Green aggregate status cannot satisfy this step when a required user-acceptance, end-to-end, integration, unit or negative-path result is missing, bound to another subject, or contradicted by a material frame result.
P6; ASSURANCE section 10

clauses.statement: For candidate_ready the Executive verifies the exact subject and decides on independent review; aggregate green cannot cover a missing or contradicted required frame result.

arguments.literal: For refused, incomplete or re_entry_requested, the Executive verifies the exact basis and applies the existing authority relation; it records the applicable disposition, or reactivates work only where current authority already permits that action. None of these variants is accepted progress because work occurred.
P6, P5

clauses.statement: For refused, incomplete or re_entry_requested the Executive records the disposition or reactivates only where authority already permits; none is accepted progress because work occurred.

arguments.literal: When independent review is not required, the Executive consumes the exact candidate, the Worker's self-review, the transition evidence and any mandatory specialist results, and applies the disposition within its decision envelope. Self-review stays Worker evidence; the disposition does not relabel it as independent.
P6

clauses.statement: Without required review the Executive disposes on Worker evidence; self-review is never relabelled independent.

arguments.literal: When independent review is required, the Executive activates the Reviewer with: the exact candidate and governing basis; the exact claim, composition boundary, population, scope and exclusions; the applicable method and project authority; the required evidence and the ordinary assurance path; the required user-acceptance, end-to-end, integration, unit, combinatorial and negative-path frame results with their exact claims and populations; the Product-selected severity scale and the exact affected Product claims; the Reviewer's capability and independence envelope; and invalidation and stop conditions.
P6, P3

clauses.statement: A required Reviewer is activated with the exact candidate, claim, authority, evidence, frame results, severity scale, envelope and stop conditions.

arguments.literal: The Reviewer returns one closed evaluation containing: frame and activation identity; the exact subject, basis, claim, scope, exclusions and evaluated population; the Reviewer actor and the independence conditions; the evidence and the ordinary assurance path acquired; the core result; findings, counterexamples and adjacent observations; for each finding, where supportable, the technical-triage fields; invalidation conditions and, where applicable, the re-entry owner. The Reviewer returns to the Executive, not to the Worker, and does not edit the candidate, direct the repair or authorise continuation.
P6, P5

clauses.statement: The Reviewer returns one closed evaluation with core result and triaged findings to the Executive, never to the Worker.

arguments.literal: The Executive verifies that every consumed result is still bound to the current subject and basis, revalidates the complete Product view and the current MVP or release mandate, applies any declared result conjunction, assigns priority, records the effect on the current promotion boundary, and acts on exactly one disposition within its grant: accept, local_repair, re_enter or reject. ACTIVATION sections 3 and 5 own each disposition, the exact accepted checkpoint and the next already-authorised bounded action. A repair creates a new candidate, and an affected review is reactivated against it. Acceptance does not widen the Product outcome or authorise an unselected successor.
P6, P5, P4b

clauses.statement: The Executive rechecks binding, mandate and conjunction, assigns priority, records the boundary effect and applies exactly one disposition.

arguments.literal: Severity neither selects priority mechanically nor blocks promotion. Priority neither erases severity nor waives a hard stop. The Executive decides blocking from the exact affected claim, the current mandate, the applicable hard stops and the Product-owned cutoff policy. An unsupported technical assessment returns through a new or refined activation rather than being silently rewritten.
P6, P1

clauses.statement: Severity does not set priority or block; priority does not erase severity or waive a hard stop; blocking follows claim, mandate, hard stops and cutoff.

arguments.literal: A step is the activation of one reference frame, or one declared active frame configuration, on an exact subject. Its context is the projection of that activated frame to the actor; the corpus or the workspace is never the context. Intake, admission, applicability and activation are distinct relations inside the step even when one invocation performs all of them.

clauses.statement: A step activates one frame or configuration on an exact subject; its context is the frame's projection, never the corpus or workspace; intake, admission, applicability and activation are distinct relations inside it.

arguments.literal: A step's output is a candidate plus its step-produced facts (judgments with evidence, residuals, observations, authority decisions, provenance) and one stop state from the result algebra.

clauses.statement: A step outputs a candidate, its step-produced facts and one stop state.

arguments.literal: A step-produced fact is a judgment, residual, observation or authority decision produced by a step that cannot be re-acquired from declared sources; an observation reproducible from declared sources is re-acquirable, is not a step-produced fact, and is governed by sufficiency, not conservation.

clauses.statement: A step-produced fact is one that cannot be re-acquired from declared sources; reproducible observations are re-acquirable and governed by sufficiency.

arguments.literal: A structural refusal is one whose source is this profile's closed structure rather than a row of the constraint table: an unknown or missing required field under the closed value contract; a missing population, hidden record, ambiguous ref, unknown record kind or undeclared field domain; a missing row, target outside its row, wrong population or sort, unresolved external target, cardinality violation, basis-relation mismatch or nested coordinate or witness defect refused at model validation; an unknown event kind, wrong payload sort, mismatched payload digest or forbidden claim or occurrence field refused at event admission; and a qualifier-record defect refused at structural admission, a ref outside the closed `ProfileRecordRef` union, resolved under a wrong population or sort or absent from its declared external domain, and a duplicate, missing, extra, reversed or mismatched edge refused at occurrence admission. Each is the refusal of a falsified structural constraint: the closed structure is the declared predicate, and the unknown kind, unknown or missing field, wrong type or mismatched edge is the counterexample that defeats it. Stop `refusal` and decision `refused` from such a source therefore map to falsified, and to invalid_basis only when the refusal carries `refuse_invalid_basis` or is emitted with an `invalid_basis` decision, as for every refusal. A required reference that `model_validation` leaves unresolved is not refused: it retains `gap` until repaired and maps to invalid_basis by that stop's row. The refusal qualifier, not the core member, records whether the defect is a missing, duplicate, wrong-typed or out-of-scope input or an invalid basis. Neither member to which `partial` and `partial_effect` map records that the subject changed. The `partial_effect` residual and its re-entry carry that fact and survive every join. Falsified never licenses treating the effect as absent; indeterminate never licenses treating it as absent or as complete; under either member the explicit re-entry precedes any further effect.
TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE, Closed constraint, judgment, residual and stop kinds; P5, P6, P4b

clauses.statement: A refusal from the closed structure is the refusal of a falsified structural constraint and maps to falsified, to invalid_basis only with refuse_invalid_basis or an invalid_basis decision; neither member for partial or partial_effect records that the subject changed; the residual does.

arguments.literal: Every substantive change, whatever its intake label, enters through one intake triage that names the smallest lawful re-entry point; triage records the change intent, the class, the re-entry point and when triage occurred, wherever substantive work begins.

clauses.statement: Every substantive change starts with triage naming its class and smallest lawful re-entry point.

arguments.literal: A reference frame may be represented in prose, structured data, a prompt, a design asset, a typed carrier, a runtime context or any other form its consumer selects. No class, aggregate, actor, controller, service, registry, graph or frame engine is required.

clauses.statement: A frame's substrate is the consumer's choice; no engine, registry, controller or carrier is required.

arguments.literal: When admission is absent or rejected, ACTIVATION section 1 returns the missing work authority without execution. Before that return, an obligation that must survive the run becomes a sprint-local entry when its lifetime stays inside the admitted sprint; otherwise it is recorded as a durable ticket, only under ticket-state authority; where that authority is absent, it is retained in the contract's named durable result and evidence surface or in an already-authorised enclosing carrier, closure is marked withheld on ticket-state authority, and the required re-entry is returned.
P4b, P6

clauses.statement: A failed admission returns the missing authority without execution, and a surviving obligation is carried by sprint entry, ticket under authority, or the named result surface.

arguments.literal: Technical triage is the Reviewer's assessment of one finding against the exact evaluated claim and basis. Where admissible evidence and the actor's capability envelope support it, it records: the affected claim and the observed failure; severity on the Product-selected severity scale; causal assessment and confidence; blast radius and the affected users, paths or relations; an available workaround or containment; repair complexity, regression risk and material dependencies; residual uncertainty and the evidence that would reduce it. Missing causal or repair evidence stays explicit; where the missing relation can change the evaluation the Reviewer returns indeterminate or out_of_frame pressure, does not invent precision and does not send work sideways to the Worker.
P6, P5

clauses.statement: The Reviewer triages each finding against the exact claim and basis, keeps missing evidence explicit and invents no precision.

arguments.literal: 1 no finite actor is presumed to hold the complete workspace in attention; 2 a useful frame is finite and sufficient for a declared evaluation family; 3 the evaluations to be made determine the material attention surface; 4 human authority may declare a practical frame set without deriving a unique partition mechanically; 5 frames may overlap, compose, refine, restrict, translate or succeed one another, hierarchy being one optional relation; 6 several frames may be used together without composing their coordinate systems; 7 coverage is relative to a declared workspace, outcome, inventory, basis and time; 8 a frame selection or result acquires no semantic, operation or decision authority from its breadth, usefulness, actor or technology; 9 unknown and out-of-frame results are lawful pressure for reconfiguration, neither failed evaluations nor implied acceptance; 10 historical failures, resets and invisible violations are evidence for improving a declaration, activation, actor assignment or frame set.
P0 to P6

clauses.statement: The ten core claims, each made precise by a law of section 3.

arguments.literal: Tenant branches, worktrees, sparse cones, snapshot binding to an input commit, authorised reviews at named commits and merge on acceptance are local development law of the stdo_3 source project, stated once in its Product Definition and imported by reference.

clauses.statement: Tenant isolation and merge are the source project's local law, stated once in its Product Definition and imported by reference.

arguments.literal: Tenant territory is imported from the same source, its Territory rule, and is not law of this method: a tenant commits only in its own territory; a needed common change is requested from the common WHAT's writing owner and reaches the tenant by merging the main lineage inward; a tenant does not edit tickets, common files or a peer tenant's realisation.

clauses.statement: Tenant territory is imported from the Product Definition and is not law of this method: a tenant commits only in its own territory and does not edit tickets, common files or a peer tenant's realisation.

arguments.literal: This member owns this law in the bounded context urn:stdo:bounded-context:semantic-resolution under the selected complete STDO basis; a glossary may index that identity and does not participate in its declaration. A term is a lexical label used in an occurrence, not a context-free concept identity. A bounded context is an explicitly identified semantic scope in which a governed vocabulary, concept set and relation set are jointly interpretable under named authority.
