A concept reference is an exact, resolvable reference to a meaning owned by an authority under a selected basis; it locates that meaning and mints neither the meaning nor its authority.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5 Bounded-context semantic resolution; P1, P3, P6

clauses.statement: A term is a label, a bounded context is an owned semantic scope, and a concept reference locates owned meaning without minting it.

arguments.literal: Every material term occurrence resolves under the semantic address (term, bounded-context identity, owning authority, selected basis, governed scope). Equal spelling, capitalisation, shape, file location, directory nesting, actor or implementation does not establish equal meaning, concept identity, equivalence, inheritance or authority; different spelling does not prove different meaning. Those relations follow only from the applicable semantic address or from an explicit authorised relation. Resolution proceeds in order: (1) identify the occurrence's governed scope and nearest explicit bounded-context declaration; (2) identify the exact selected basis and the authorities applicable to that context and scope; (3) collect the context-local definitions and the explicitly imported concept references admitted by those authorities and that basis; (4) apply every applicable owner-authorised override or disambiguation; (5) admit the occurrence only when exactly one concept remains.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5 Bounded-context semantic resolution; P1, P3, P5

clauses.statement: Each material occurrence resolves by its semantic address through five ordered steps and is admitted only when exactly one concept remains.

arguments.literal: A worked application, a hello world or a data mapper is an external test subject; its particulars cannot become generic method functionality by precedent.

clauses.statement: A test subject's particulars cannot become generic method functionality by precedent.

arguments.literal: One execution may provide several bound results. A supported user scenario may supply user-acceptance evidence for the outcome, end-to-end evidence for the runnable causal path, integration evidence for selected seams and unit counterexamples for a module-owned algebra. Those claims stay distinct and combine only through declared REFERENCE_FRAME §6 relations. The default proof responsibilities are: user acceptance proves the outcome from the user's supported frame; end to end proves the complete authoritative runnable Product path; integration proves material participant composition; and unit proves module-owned laws, with evidence size and strategy proportional to their internal combinatorial complexity. Integration and unit results cannot stand in for either broader claim. When the Product claim requires all of them, a conflict or a missing result stays visible to the decision owner's disposition and cannot be hidden by aggregate green status.
P4a, P6, P5

clauses.statement: Testing results stay bound to their claims; a missing or conflicting required result cannot be hidden by aggregate green.

arguments.literal: A test file, suite, runner, fixture, scenario label, coverage percentage or actor does not become a testing frame by existing. A testing frame's authority is bounded by the claim actually exercised; test count, assertion count, source coverage, runtime duration and framework category do not widen it. Producing an expected output through a bypass, an obsolete executor, a test-only seam, an undeclared fallback or a competing authority falsifies path conformance even when the output value is equal.

clauses.statement: A testing frame's authority is bounded by the claim exercised; a bypass falsifies path conformance even with equal output.

arguments.literal: Frame disjointness is structural; evaluation independence is procedural; assurance independence is claim-relative and stated by the governing assurance law (EVALUATION section 3). Disjoint frames need not be independently evaluated; independently activated evaluations need not be disjoint; and the unqualified word independent establishes none of the three.
P6, P1

clauses.statement: Disjointness (structural), evaluation independence (procedural) and assurance independence (claim-relative) stay distinct; the bare word independent establishes none.

arguments.literal: Ticket type answers what kind of work record this is; change class answers where the change lawfully re-enters the constitutional chain; ticket_category governs execution and closure discipline. A ticket records the change_class declared by intake triage. Common pairings: feature with goal_reprice, intent_reprice, product_reprice, requirement_reprice or design_reframe; bug with requirement_reprice, design_reframe or realization_refactor; chore with design_reframe or realization_refactor; spike carries the current triage class.
P4b, P2, P3

clauses.statement: Type, change class and category are orthogonal; the ticket records the class intake triage declared.

arguments.literal: "Ticket-shaped" describes the categorisation, closure criteria, proof surface, non-closure conditions and the other required execution-contract fields. It creates no durable ticket identity and no ticket-lane state.
P3

clauses.statement: A ticket-shaped contract creates no durable ticket identity or lane state.

arguments.literal: A state-value change preserves the frame topology only when it preserves every entity, relation, lifecycle, authority, capability, adjacency and seam; a transition that changes any of them is a topology mutation that may invalidate the frame's coordinates. A frame need not hold the workspace's complete topology.
P3

clauses.statement: A change that alters any entity, relation, lifecycle, authority, capability, adjacency or seam is a topology mutation; a frame need not hold the whole topology.

arguments.literal: Total handling does not claim that every external condition is recognised, that an invoked provider terminates, or that every request can be completed. A hanging external call, an unsatisfiable demand and a lost post-effect response are three different cases and none is solved by adding a value to the algebra.

clauses.statement: Total handling claims no omniscience; a hanging call, an unsatisfiable demand and a lost response are different cases not solved by a new algebra value.

arguments.literal: Every transformation records what it preserved, introduced and removed, its external resolution witnesses and its residuals.

clauses.statement: Every transformation records preserved, introduced, removed, witnesses and residuals.

arguments.literal: Admission of a material transition is one semantic commit of the complete transition within its enclosing relation, or none.

clauses.statement: A material transition is admitted as one complete semantic commit within its enclosing relation, or not at all.

arguments.literal: One frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another. The translation declares source and target coordinates, preserved meaning, accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions.
P1, P4b

clauses.statement: A translation declares source and target coordinates, preserved meaning, accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions.

arguments.literal: The core stop kinds are hold, gap, refusal, invalid_basis, out_of_scope and partial_effect. Every constraint predicate returns exactly one of satisfied, falsified, indeterminate or invalid_basis. satisfied maps to the judgment's positive decision, the first decision it lists; invalid_basis maps only to invalid_basis; the constraint table fixes every other mapping. An implementation cannot turn an omitted result, a residual or a stop into success.
TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE, Closed constraint, judgment, residual and stop kinds; P5, P6

clauses.statement: Six stop kinds; every constraint predicate returns satisfied, falsified, indeterminate or invalid_basis; no omitted result, residual or stop becomes success.

arguments.literal: Default total mapping to the five core members, adding none (ACTIVATION §3 one-algebra rule; AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5 requires a traversal's stop algebra to map totally). Each stop kind and judgment decision, read with the source and qualifier of a refusal and, for stop partial_effect and decision partial, with what the effect evidence and the bounded post-observation establish, maps to exactly one core member, keeping its own vocabulary, residual and re-entry law. stop hold -> indeterminate: the deciding evidence is not yet admitted while every relation and capability the judgment requires is declared and was exercised (ACTIVATION §3, second case); its residual names the evidence that would decide. stop gap -> invalid_basis: a reference or lineage member the judgment requires is unresolved, so the basis cannot support the judgment until repaired. stop refusal -> invalid_basis only when the refusal carries refuse_invalid_basis or is emitted with an invalid_basis decision; falsified for every other refusal, which follows a falsified constraint and carries refuse_missing, refuse_duplicate, refuse_wrong_type or refuse_out_of_scope, the defect it names being the counterexample: a row of the constraint table, a structural constraint, or the requirement that an admitted event carry a lawful declared scope, whose refusal of admission under the unresolved_scope re-entry carries refuse_missing. stop invalid_basis -> invalid_basis. stop out_of_scope -> falsified: emitted only with refusal, when event_scope_compatible is falsified by a declared scope that conflicts with the admitting authority; an event scope not yet declared is hold plus unresolved_scope, the spelling is not the core's out_of_frame, and a refusal of admission once that re-entry closes without the declaration is stop refusal carrying refuse_missing, not this stop. stop partial_effect -> falsified when the effect evidence establishes that the effect has ended and the bounded post-observation shows part of the intended outcome not reached, the unreached part being the counterexample; otherwise indeterminate (by the stop-state route of construction availability's incomplete where the bounded post-observation is not yet acquired; as ACTIVATION §3's second case where it is acquired and still cannot decide). transition_evaluation partial -> the same rule. transition_evaluation refused -> under the rule of stop refusal: invalid_basis only when its refusal carries refuse_invalid_basis; otherwise falsified. Remaining judgment decisions: the first decision each judgment lists -> satisfied; refused, out_of_scope, unauthorized and stale -> falsified, save that refused maps to invalid_basis only when its refusal carries refuse_invalid_basis; hold -> indeterminate; gap -> invalid_basis; invalid_basis and transition_evaluation's falsified and indeterminate -> the members so named. A traversal record's stop_states may refine which of hold, gap and refusal map to which non-satisfied member, by a binding declared in the PROFILES §1 shape (direction, preserved meaning, narrowed scope, invalidation); the other stops and every judgment decision keep this mapping, and a record that declares no binding takes the default. A judgment decision is the evaluation's result and a stop is the step's; where values emitted together map to different members, as stale with hold does, each answers its own question.

clauses.statement: Stops and judgment decisions map totally to the core: hold indeterminate; gap and invalid_basis invalid_basis; refusal falsified, and invalid_basis only when it carries refuse_invalid_basis or comes with an invalid_basis decision; out_of_scope falsified; partial_effect and partial falsified or indeterminate by the effect evidence; the decision is the evaluation's result, the stop the step's.

arguments.literal: A ticket for substantive work carries the minimum metadata required by intake triage: the declared change_intent, the lawful change_class, the lawful re_entry_point, and when triage occurred in triaged_at. The recorded values are those intake triage declared.
P4b, P2

clauses.statement: Substantive-work tickets carry change_intent, change_class, re_entry_point and triaged_at as triage declared them.

arguments.literal: Triage triangulates a failure across the applicable reference frames over the same subject and basis; their combined results constrain the supported cause, preserve unresolved alternatives and uncertainty, and identify the smallest sufficient lawful scope of repair. The frame that exposes a failure need not contain its cause. Repeating the same analysis under different frame names supplies no additional causal evidence. A diagnosis grants no repair effects and does not establish that governing meaning must change: a candidate may instead need correction under sufficient existing law.
P6

clauses.statement: Triage triangulates across applicable frames on one subject and basis; the exposing frame need not hold the cause and a diagnosis grants no repair.

arguments.literal: Trials declare a per-actor context cap and total-work budget before each run, include a required basis larger than the cap, count transferred context across every delegated actor, keep acceptance criteria independent of the constructing actor, and repeat probabilistic trials with varied task order.

clauses.statement: Trials declare cap and budget first, exceed the cap in required basis, count context across actors, keep criteria independent and repeat with varied order.

arguments.literal: The wider typed-lineage graph may lawfully contain opposing edges of different kinds: one event may support another while the second corrects the first. A cycle in the untyped union is not a causal cycle unless one declared causal subgraph itself cycles.
TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE, Causality and typed lineage; P3

clauses.statement: Opposing lineage edges of different kinds are lawful; only a cycle within one declared causal subgraph is a causal cycle.

arguments.literal: For required obligations R and admitted coverage C, uncovered coverage is R minus C; combining results takes the union of known failures and recomputes uncovered coverage.

clauses.statement: Uncovered coverage is R minus C; combination unions failures and recomputes uncovered coverage.

arguments.literal: A term the claim depends on and the frame leaves undefined is an undeclared material relation: its meaning can alter the result and it enters through no declared input. A claim that depends on such a term is out_of_frame on the ground of the missing declaration.

clauses.statement: A term the claim depends on that the frame leaves undefined is an undeclared material relation, and the claim is out_of_frame.

arguments.literal: unresolved: the only other state; it blocks qualification of the affected claim.

clauses.statement: An unresolved predecessor claim blocks qualification of the affected claim; the disposition values are UP-015's, applied to the corpus itself.

arguments.literal: no member of its own when the step did not exercise a declared capability the evaluation requires. A result is returned wherever a sufficient evaluation or an applicable judgment exists without that capability, identifying its evidence, verdict and residual uncertainty like any closed result (rc.2 RF #rf-012-closed-results, #return-a-closed-result): a counterexample found by what was exercised, as when source inspection falsifies A in a claim of A and B, returns falsified, and common agreement cannot discard it (rc.2 RF #result-conjunction). Where none exists because the capability was not exercised, there is no result for that evaluation: the step's stop state carries it, incomplete under the construction availability refinement below, and its work state (§5) carries the unexercised capability as a residual (P6; an actor cannot report an evaluation it did not perform). In either case the unexercised part, B above, is an uncovered required obligation, never a result: an absent required result cannot satisfy a dependent conjunction, and a missing mandatory result remains unresolved (rc.2 RF #applicability-and-required-results, #result-conjunction); a known failure A and an uncovered obligation B survive every join (FOUNDATIONS §4). The evaluation's result and the step's stop state answer different questions (§1, Output), so the mapping of incomplete to the core does not make the evaluation indeterminate. The third is a tightening the predecessor implies and does not state: RF-012, Return A Closed Result, Applicability And Required Results and Result Conjunction together return what a sufficient evaluation supports and leave the unexercised part open.
P5, P6; rc.2 RF #applicability-and-required-results

clauses.statement: When a step did not exercise a declared capability the evaluation requires, there is no member of its own: a result is returned wherever a sufficient evaluation or applicable judgment exists without it; where none exists there is no result, the stop state is incomplete and the work state carries the unexercised capability as a residual; the unexercised part is an uncovered required obligation, never a result.

arguments.literal: There is one front door for substantive change. The intake label does not determine the process class: a reported bug, feature request, issue, regression, operator finding, release blocker or scenario failure all enter through the same intake triage. No bug, feature, issue or other intake bypasses this triage by going straight to code, tests or release handling.
P2, P6

clauses.statement: Every substantive intake, whatever its label, enters one intake triage; none goes straight to code, tests or release.

arguments.literal: Unknown treatment withholds dependent reliance or promotion, not unrelated authorised work. An existing bounded construction or evidence grant may permit the cheapest useful discriminator without asserting that the candidate is conformant. A mistaken route is corrected at its smallest affected owner, preserving the original cause, the attempted subject, the observed effect state and valid progress; an unknown effect state cannot be silently treated as no effect.
P5

clauses.statement: Unknown treatment withholds dependent reliance or promotion only; a mistaken route is corrected at its smallest affected owner.

arguments.literal: Triage consumes the computed classification for the declared owner and layer traversal, the complete relevant public membership and value delta, the accepted-design scope and trace coverage, and the rule-determined treatment. The owning work carrier references that exact result and its residuals; a new role does not repeat an unchanged walk.
P4b, P2

clauses.statement: The upward check consumes the computed classification; the carrier references it and a new role does not repeat an unchanged walk.

arguments.literal: The walk goes upward to the first missing layer. If the governing requirement is missing or insufficient, re-enter its owner. If that requirement is sufficient but the realising design is missing or insufficient, re-enter Design. Follow an actual upstream Goal, Intent or Product change to its owner rather than stopping at a familiar file. When the current requirement and accepted design suffice and the implementation deviates, repair or reject the candidate under realization_refactor. A candidate's public violation does not select a new contract. An explicitly changed desired outcome or an established governing insufficiency follows the owning re-entry; unresolved meaning remains J and a reserved choice remains O.
P2, P6

clauses.statement: The upward walk re-enters the owner of the first missing or insufficient layer; with requirement and design sufficient, the candidate is repaired or rejected.

arguments.literal: A project adopts the profile by: naming it in its UX-related design modules; recording the realisation stack choice and justification; declaring the irreducible architectural carrier set and structural carrier diagram (DESIGN_MODULE §6, §7); declaring the State, Msg, Update, Cmd and Sub shapes for each UX surface in the design module before implementation; declaring the typed-contract bindings the surface consumes and emits to (§7); naming the effect-membrane mechanism and the Cmd algebra it interprets (§6); naming the executable Msg-replay proof surface (§8); naming any §11 accessibility refinement; noting any §9 view-shape or §6 effect-membrane exemptions explicitly. Adoption is per project and may cover only some UX surfaces, with the scope recorded in the design module.
UX §12; P2, P4b, P6

clauses.statement: Adoption records the stack, the per-surface process-model shapes, the membrane and Cmd algebra, the replay proof surface and any exemptions in the design module.

arguments.literal: Side effects are isolated to a declared effect membrane, which refines DESIGN_MODULE §10 Effect edge for UX surfaces. The membrane interprets Cmd values produced by the reducer and translates side-effect outcomes back into Msg values delivered to the reducer. Inside the membrane, I/O, subscriptions to external sources and imperative interop with the host platform (DOM, file system, native APIs) are allowed. Outside it, in render code, in pure helpers consumed by render, and in the reducer, there is no I/O, no subscription and no imperative platform manipulation.
UX §6; P0, P5

clauses.statement: No I/O, subscription or imperative platform manipulation outside the declared membrane; effects return to the reducer as Msg.

arguments.literal: The membrane has one job: interpret declared Cmd values; it is not where logic lives. Branching, conditional state derivation and multi-step business decisions belong in the reducer; the membrane interprets a single declared Cmd per effect. A platform-specific effect handler, whatever the framework calls it (useEffect, createEffect, onMount, subscribe, a server-action handler), is part of the membrane only when it interprets a declared Cmd. A handler that contains conditional logic deciding state transitions is a violation: the logic moves to the reducer, and the handler interprets one Cmd.
UX §6; P1, P6

clauses.statement: An effect handler belongs to the membrane only when it interprets one declared Cmd; a handler that decides state transitions is a violation.

arguments.literal: Every product UX surface carries at least one executable Msg-replay proof for each product-meaningful interaction family before claiming closure under this profile. A replay proof includes: an initial State fixture; an ordered Msg log; the expected final State; the expected ordered Cmd values; the success and failure Msg values returned by interpreted Cmds; injected deterministic values for time, randomness, generated ids and external payloads. The proof fails if correctness depends on: DOM state not represented in State; mutable refs, module variables, closures, timers or effect-handler memory; network or file results that bypass typed Msg; view-local state that changes product behaviour after unmount or replay. For a pure projection-only surface the proof may be a no-effect proof: a Msg log, the final State and an empty Cmd sequence.
UX §8 Msg-replay proof; P2, P4b, P5, P6

clauses.statement: Before claiming closure, every product UX surface carries at least one executable Msg-replay proof per product-meaningful interaction family, with the listed parts and none of the listed dependencies; a pure projection-only surface may use a no-effect proof.

arguments.literal: The constitutional process model of UX work is the Elm Architecture. State: the typed state shape, held by the runtime, not by the view. Msg: the typed message algebra naming every action a user or system can emit. Update: the pure reducer (Msg, State) -> (State, Cmd); it describes side effects as Cmd values and does not perform them. View: the pure function State -> ViewTree; the same state gives the same output. Cmd and Sub: typed descriptions of side effects to schedule and of external sources to subscribe to, interpreted by the runtime at the effect membrane. The runtime owns the loop: current State -> render View -> user emits Msg -> Update produces new State and Cmds -> runtime interprets Cmds -> repeat.
UX §4; P0, P1

clauses.statement: The process model is the Elm Architecture: pure Update and View, effects described as Cmd and Sub, the loop owned by the runtime.

arguments.literal: UX is the UX profile. It refines DESIGN_MODULE for modules that realise a UX surface, imports the core, and binds: the Elm process model with typed State, Msg, Update, View, Cmd and Sub; the boundary between UX messages and admitted product carriers; the state transition law; the effect membrane; binding to AssetSurface or an equivalent typed contract; view continuation and the Msg-replay proof; view shape; type sharing with runtime validation at untrusted seams; the accessibility minimum; realisation discretion; adoption with the scaffold and exemption law and UX sprint compliance escrow; the failure patterns and review questions; and the total mapping of its verdicts to the core algebra (UX §15).

clauses.statement: UX is the UX profile; it refines DESIGN_MODULE for modules that realise a UX surface, imports the core and restates UX_METHOD in full.

arguments.literal: Each verdict answers its own question and maps as stated; nothing is coerced to satisfied. (1) compliant: do §4 to §10 hold under inspection with no §13 failure pattern present -> satisfied (this row applies the stricter of two compliance tests that disagree, §4 Realisation discretion against the §12 compliance criterion; the choice is pending Jim's ruling and is not settled by the mapping). (2) violation, including constitutionally rejected (§4): is a §13 failure pattern present -> falsified, the pattern present being the counterexample. (3) replay proof passes or fails (§8): does the proof reproduce the expected final State and Cmd sequence without a dependency §8 lists -> satisfied when it passes, falsified when it fails. (4) closure claimed without the §8 proof or the §11 obligations (§12): does every product-meaningful interaction family carry its proof and the surface its accessibility declarations, absent a recorded exemption -> falsified, the family or obligation without proof being the counterexample; inside an open UX sprint the gap is escrow and closure is not claimed. (5) blocked for want of a carrier (§3, §7): does a product-truth-changing message or action have an admitted carrier or typed contract -> the surface's evaluation is falsified (§13 pattern 13); the construction step stops as ACTIVATION §3 re_entry_requested, core out_of_frame, naming the missing carrier, its owner and the re-entry. (6) fails closed (§1 Authority): is the surface compliant where the profile is ambiguous for the case -> the stricter reading's result where that reading is fixed; out_of_frame where the ambiguity leaves a term the claim depends on undefined, naming the term and its owner; indeterminate only where the stricter reading is fixed and admissible evidence cannot decide; never satisfied by the ambiguity alone. (7) design module incomplete (§14): can each review question be answered from the design module -> invalid_basis. Collisions: blocked for want of a carrier is not ACTIVATION §3's ambiguity outcome blocked; design module incomplete is not the construction availability member incomplete.
UX §15; the one-algebra rule of ACTIVATION §3; P1, P5, P6

clauses.statement: Every UX profile verdict maps totally to one core member and adds none.

arguments.literal: A scaffold, prototype, debug pane or temporary proof surface may be exempt only when the design module or ticket records all of: the exemption scope; the permitted operations; whether mutation is forbidden or explicitly bounded; a visible scaffold or debug label where user-facing; the authoritative surface that will supersede it; the retirement condition and owning ticket; the non-closure condition preventing release if the scaffold remains. An exempt scaffold cannot become the production UX by accumulation: it is retired, repriced into a governed UX surface, or kept outside product closure. An exempt scaffold is a recorded scope, not a result; evaluations outside its recorded scope proceed under the §15 table.
UX §12 Scaffold and exemption, §15; P4b, P6

clauses.statement: Exemption needs all seven recorded items; without them the surface stays governed, and an exempt scaffold never becomes production UX by accumulation.

arguments.literal: The implementation stack (language, framework or runtime, state container, effect-interpreter mechanism, runtime validator, toolchain) is the project's choice, recorded in its design module with a short justification of how each choice preserves the §4 process model and the §6 effect-membrane rule; the profile does not rank stacks, it tests realisations. Constitutionally rejected, regardless of stack: a realisation that lets the view own state continuation, performs side effects in render code, mutates state outside a typed reducer, or carries multi-step view-local state machines that bypass Msg; two-way binding without Msg emission, imperative DOM manipulation in render code, and effect handlers used as controllers are violations. Compliance: §4 Process model without stack mandate says any realisation that preserves §4 to §8 is compliant; §4 Realisation discretion says a realisation is compliant when §4 to §10 hold under inspection and the §13 failure patterns are absent.
UX §4 Process model without stack mandate, §4 Realisation discretion; P1, P2, P6

clauses.statement: The stack is free and recorded with its justification; a realisation that breaks the process model is rejected whatever its stack.

arguments.literal: A UX surface is governed by this profile by default when any of these is true: it is reachable from the product shell; it is used as proof for a ticket, requirement, design module, release or review; it can mutate product truth; it can spawn, attach, resume or dispatch work; it can change Context, selection authority, closure, continuation, evidence or provenance.
UX §12 Scaffold and exemption; P5, P6

clauses.statement: Any one of the five triggers makes a surface governed by default.

arguments.literal: The view does not own state continuation; state transitions flow through declared Msg actions interpreted by the reducer. A view does not decide on its own what the next state will be after a user event; does not chain several state updates locally without emitting them as separate Msg values; does not carry hidden inter-event state in refs, closures or module-level variables. A multi-step local state machine belongs in the reducer as part of State, with explicit Msg transitions between phases; the view becomes a pure projection of its phase. The Msg-replay test: can the view's behaviour be replayed by replaying its Msg log against an empty State? If not, continuation has leaked into the view.
UX §8; P0, P1, P4b, P6

clauses.statement: The view never owns continuation; if replaying the Msg log against an empty State does not reproduce its behaviour, continuation has leaked.

arguments.literal: A Σ admits materially different behaviours.
It either declares the latitude or is repaired before a decision-complete design is claimed.

clauses.statement: A weak Σ declares its latitude or is repaired before decision-complete design is claimed.

arguments.literal: Packaging, syntax, compilation, presence, invocation or local behaviour never substitutes for a semantic, authority-bearing, installed, release or end-to-end claim because the weaker property is easier to measure.

clauses.statement: A weaker property never substitutes for the claimed one because it is easier to measure.

arguments.literal: A product definition's what bindings locate the shared constitutional WHAT; its how.build_tenants bindings locate one or more independent realisations. Tenant-local realisation is derivative until its governing truth is ratified in specification.

clauses.statement: What bindings locate the shared WHAT; tenant bindings locate independent HOWs, derivative until ratified.

arguments.literal: The result references the current computed classification, supporting evidence, residual judgments and original rulings through their existing carriers; it does not reconstruct unchanged C/J/O at each handoff. arguments.literal: It exists only after a successful Worker activation. An activation_refusal (REFERENCE_FRAME §5) returns to the assigning authority or declared result carrier and creates neither a Worker activation nor a Worker result. candidate_ready (with satisfied): an exact candidate and its transition evidence are available; refused (with falsified): lawful activation occurred, and a governing prohibition or an owner-valid construction refusal defeats the requested construction; incomplete (with indeterminate): the valid activation produced no candidate because admissible evidence or bounded execution cannot yet decide or complete the relation; and re_entry_requested (with out_of_frame or invalid_basis): a material decision lies outside Worker authority, or the activated basis can no longer support the work. The mapping is total and exclusive after lawful activation. Payload wording, stop timing or actor preference cannot select another variant.

arguments.literal: Work state is the tuple of: the current persistent workspace; the governing basis; the applicable closed results and judgments with their invalidators; the residuals; and the known uncertainty over external effects. It is an object; its carrier (files, an event stream, another admitted owner) is a profile or realisation choice.

arguments.literal: Every product-outcome-bearing work wave identifies one explicitly selected, unresolved, directly verifiable product-defined outcome and declares the acceptance interval for that instance. Product-progress claims and promotion onto the supported product path are judged against that same outcome. Evidence distinguishes material advance, prerequisite readiness, preservation and regression. Only material advance projects product progress. Prerequisite work names the product obligation it enables and remains bounded. Preservation is useful evidence, not progress. A regression or unresolved gap blocks further promotion on the affected path until repaired, repriced or accepted by the owning authority.

clauses.statement: Every product-outcome-bearing work wave identifies one explicitly selected, unresolved, directly verifiable outcome and its acceptance interval; product-progress claims are judged against it.

arguments.literal: WORLD_MODEL is the world-model profile. It imports the core and binds: the imported product-lineage concepts and the Builder Project specialisation; the Markov-object construct at candidate status with its effective blanket, working refinements, epistemic status and promotion gate; the core claims and units; entity recovery and the entity cut as the published identity-bearing unit, with its admissibility, discrimination and publication law; the attribute ledger; the representation, materialisation and publication laws; Markov-object overlay construction; saturation; composition of local artifacts; projection; the control and data planes; the proof law and world-model-driven development; and the total mapping of its verdicts to the core algebra (WORLD_MODEL §14). Nothing in the core depends on the construct being established.

arguments.literal: Each verdict answers its own question; nothing is coerced to satisfied. (1) admissible entity cut (§9): are the eight surfaces explicit, traceable and discriminated at evidence altitude proportional to the claim -> satisfied; a stated bound on evidence altitude with its residual ambiguity declared satisfies the test. (2) entity cut not admissible (§9): is a surface neither a stated value, a stated absence nor a stated non-applicability, or untraceable, or undiscriminated -> falsified, the surface being the counterexample; indeterminate only where the discrimination the cut itself claims cannot be decided at its stated altitude. (3) verified overlay direction (§10) -> satisfied. (4) inadmissible extraction, a principal-component or maximum-variance construction (§10) -> falsified whatever its verification. (5) failed verification (§10) -> falsified. (6) inconclusive verification (§10): did a recorded verification run without establishing either an acceptable preservation or a demonstrated loss of identity -> indeterminate, naming the held-out treatment or verification that would decide (ACTIVATION §3, second case). (7) candidate direction, no verification run (§10) -> no evaluation result: unresolved under ACTIVATION §3's third case; the step that left it unrun stops incomplete, core indeterminate; publishing the direction is falsified for the publication claim. (8) not yet a lawful Markov object (§10): satisfied when the uniqueness and transfer tests both pass, falsified when either fails. (9) overlay with no declared representation space, or directions composed across spaces -> invalid_basis. (10) promotion gate (§4): satisfied when met; falsified for that gate run when not met; the construct's standing is unchanged. (11) sufficiently saturated (§11): do material attributes have traceable support with remaining gaps explicit -> satisfied, the explicit gaps carried as residuals; falsified where an attribute exists without support. (12) storage layout (§10): satisfied when the six surfaces are retained; falsified when any is lost. Candidate-class and established are standings of the construct, and candidate-class and formally closed are publication kinds; none is a result.
WORLD_MODEL §14; the one-algebra rule of ACTIVATION §3; P1, P5, P6

residuals.detail: PROFILES section 3 conserves DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD by reference, which requires the ontology-first derivation chain where it applies, while ACTIVATION section 6 asks every obligation to pay for the ambiguity it removes. Whether a design boundary with no material alternative must still pay the full chain is not decided by this corpus; it is a question for the profile's owner.

The envelope has four dimensions (context, attention, time, capability). The context dimension is measured in bytes before any read; attention, time and capability have no measure or declaration format, and the documents do not say how a step records that the test was performed on those dimensions.

The categories A, I and C_H and the functors S and R_H are named with their interpretation and established properties but not constructed in this corpus; the fragment and its non-faithfulness result are new here and rest on the accepted C1 realisation's argument, which the standard does not carry; rc.2 states only the proof obligation. The program records the claim's shape, not a proof.

Each independent commitment carries a one-sentence non-entailment argument in its qualification. These are claims of independence with an informal witness each; none is formalised and P4a states none. The accepted C1 realisation argues them at greater length; the standard conserves only the sentence.

SPEC_METHOD section 11 imports the stdo_3 Product Definition's Development Isolation rules by reference. That document is outside this program's source basis, so the imported obligations are a route in the document, not clauses here.

Every encoded clause's rc.2 disposition is carried in the documents as a route, not in this program: the program's source basis is the tenant standards directory and rc.2 members are outside it. Conservation of an rc.2 clause therefore cannot be checked by this program's validation; it remains a semantic judgment over the documents and their routes.
